01 — SOURCING & RESEARCH

How I source and research leads

I start with Apollo to build a prospect list, then cross-check each company using Google Search, Maps, LinkedIn, and company websites before adding it to the database.

Apollo company research

I review industry, employee count, keywords, company details, and other scale signals.

Google Search & Maps

I check location, business type, public listings, and whether the company appears relevant to the target niche.

Company website verification

I confirm what the business actually does instead of relying only on a database industry label.

Why manual verification matters: Apollo can classify irrelevant companies under “Real Estate.” I cross-check the company’s website and public information before deciding whether a prospect should move forward.
02 — ORGANIZING THE DATA

One master lead database

After research, I organize each lead in one Google Sheets database so company, contact, email, verification, and outreach information stays consistent.

  • 1
    Company data
    Company name, niche, location, company snapshot, website, and website status.
  • 2
    Decision-maker data
    Contact person, job title, decision-maker email, gatekeeper/company email, and backup contacts.
  • 3
    Verification
    I track whether emails are verified, not verified, or still need checking.
  • 4
    Workflow status
    Records move through verification and GHL preparation instead of staying as a raw list.
Public portfolio version: client and contact details are redacted while the real database structure is preserved.
Master Lead Database

03 — QUALIFICATION & READINESS

Only clean leads move forward

I qualify companies against the client’s ICP, verify the business type, find the right decision-maker, track email status, and prepare organized records for handoff.

  • 1
    Check ICP fit
    Does the company match the target niche and campaign criteria?
  • 2
    Verify business type
    For real estate, I distinguish true owners/investors from agents, brokers, and non-owner property managers.
  • 3
    Assess scale
    When revenue is unavailable, I use employee count, portfolio, locations, founding year, and public company signals.
  • 4
    Find the right contact
    Founder, president, principal, managing partner, CFO, controller, or another relevant decision-maker.
  • 5
    Prepare for handoff
    Qualified records move into verification and GHL upload preparation.
Qualification inside the database

The master sheet keeps research and readiness in one place instead of relying on separate notes.

04 — WORKFLOW IMPROVEMENT

Custom Add Lead tool

With 2,000+ records in a single sheet, entering data directly across a very wide database becomes slow and error-prone. I created an Add Lead tool using Google Apps Script to make the process easier.

1. Open the tool

Access it directly from Lead Tools → Add New Lead.

3. Keep the workflow organized

The lead database feeds a structured workflow for verification and GHL preparation.

2. Enter data in one guided form

Instead of scrolling across many columns, I can enter a lead through one sidebar. The client example is redacted for confidentiality.

I created the Add Lead tool using scripting to make 2,000+ record data entry easier.

It reduces manual scrolling, standardizes how information is entered, and makes a high-volume lead database easier to maintain. A second script formats every verified lead to GoHighLevel's import fields, so the upload queue is ready in one step, with no manual reformatting.
